name: Throat
author: E. T. Carter
description: An ice-cave throat swallowing the view: concentric shelves of translucent ice with organic noise-displaced contours, cold rim light pooling in the bays, hue sliding through the palette by depth, and an exponential gullet of true black at center. Shelves and their frozen wobble descend the scale axis forever — a continuous zoom that never arrives.

params.label: Descent speed
params.effect: Scale-octaves per second the ice shelves are swallowed toward the center.

params.label: Wobble
params.effect: Amplitude of the organic contour displacement; 0 gives clean circular ice rings.

params.label: Shelf density
params.effect: Number of ice shelves per scale octave.

params.label: Ice glow
params.effect: Brightness of the cold rim light along each shelf edge.

params.label: Focal X
params.effect: Horizontal offset of the throat's focal point — slide the gullet off-centre for an asymmetric, off-axis descent.

params.label: Focal Y
params.effect: Vertical offset of the throat's focal point — drop or raise the gullet out of dead-centre.

params.label: Mouse parallax
params.effect: How far the focal point glides toward the pointer for a smooth look-around (0 locks it; no effect on the static poster).
